subject: Career
title: The Strength of Dormant Ties
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Strength of Dormant Ties.

hook.text: Your most valuable contacts may be people you haven't spoken to in years. Dormant ties are hidden gold.

buildup.text: Dormant ties are former connections — ex-colleagues, old classmates — you've lost touch with.

discovery.text: Levin et al. found dormant ties provide more novel information than current contacts because they've diverged.

twist.text: Reactivating a dormant tie is easier than making a new one. The trust foundation still exists.

climax.text: Reconnect with genuine curiosity: 'I saw your post and wondered what you're working on.' Simple and authentic.

punchline.text: Old connections aren't dead connections. They're sleeping assets.

quiz.question: Why are dormant ties valuable?
options: They provide more novel information than current contacts

details.summary: Dormant ties combine the trust of an existing relationship with the information novelty of a distant contact. This dual advantage makes them uniquely powerful for career transitions, job searches, and creative problem-solving.
details.whyItMatters: Active ties share your current information bubble. Dormant ties have evolved independently and now bridge different knowledge ecosystems, offering perspectives your inner circle lacks.
takeaways: Dormant ties blend familiarity with fresh perspectives
They are especially valuable during career transitions and pivots
Maintaining a list of dormant contacts makes reactivation easier

faq.question: Why are dormant ties more useful than active ties for finding new opportunities?
faq.answer: Active ties share your information environment, so their leads overlap with what you already know. Dormant ties have moved through different industries and circles, giving them access to opportunities and perspectives outside your current ecosystem.

faq.question: How often should you audit your network for dormant ties worth reactivating?
faq.answer: Every six to twelve months, review your old contacts and identify five to ten people worth reconnecting with. Timing it with career milestones like a new role, project launch, or industry shift gives you a natural reason to reach out.
